SMTO-EXE-0226 — SMTO couldn't find that Docker network

GUID: 2441aeae-4693-5d0c-aeef-e3eb9a4349c2
Slug: docker-network-not-found
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • No Docker network (a private link Docker uses so containers can talk to each other) with exactly that name or ID exists on the Gateway computer right now. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to list the Docker networks on that Gateway, and check the exact name you used. The name must match exactly, or you can use the network's full ID.
  2. If an earlier request created or removed this network, look at that list to see what actually happened before asking for another change. A network that was removed, or recreated with a new ID, no longer matches the old name or ID.
  3. Check that you picked the Gateway for the computer where the network exists, and only ask SMTO to create a new network if your task really needs one. Each computer's Docker has its own networks, and SMTO looks only on the Gateway you selected.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finds the network by its exact name or ID and the connection or removal goes ahead.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the network name, to the person who manages Docker on that computer.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Exact network resolution on the Gateway found no network whose complete ID or exact name matches, or the Docker Engine returned 404 on a /networks endpoint.

What this means

  • Exact network lookup found no matching complete ID/name, or the Engine returned a network-path not-found response. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Exact network lookup found no matching complete ID/name, or the Engine returned a network-path not-found response.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect current network identities and any preceding network mutation on the same Engine.

How to fix it

  • List networks on the same Gateway (docker network ls --no-trunc as the Gateway account) and use the complete network ID or exact name. Check the result of any earlier network_create or network_remove before requesting another change.
  • Correct the network reference using current inventory; reconcile earlier creation/removal before another mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact object identity, typed arguments and selected Gateway capability; correct the reported prerequisite before a new request.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended network resolves exactly before a connection or removal action.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
